notes.text: **Columns: minimum and maximum.** Each table holds a set range of columns beside its first column, so cells keep enough width for their content on desktop.

Table: MarketingTable · First column: Row headings · Min: 1 · Max: 3 · Why the max: Cells hold full phrases. With 3 columns each keeps about 250px of text and wraps to two lines; a fourth drops that to about 190px, so cells run to four or five lines and rows go uneven.

Table: FeatureMatrix · First column: Qualys · Min: 1 competitor · Max: 5 competitors · Why the max: Cells are only ticks and crosses, so it takes the most columns. Past five, the logos and subtitles in the column headers get cramped.

Table: DetailComparison · First column: Qualys · Min: 1 competitor · Max: 3 competitors · Why the max: Each cell is a short paragraph (up to about 250 characters). Qualys plus three gives four columns of about 280px; a fifth would drop them to about 230px and make rows very tall. The chips tell readers "Choose up to 3".

why.text: developers need the column limits where they choose a table
